newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe see popularity at record low - poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe see popularity at record low - poll.

text.p: The popularity of French Prime Minister Alain Juppe has hit a record low and that of President Jacques Chirac has also sunk further, according to an opinion poll published on Thursday.
The centre-right government has been buffeted by rising unemployment and mounting dissent on coalition backbenches over austerity policies imposed to qualify France for a single European currency.

The Louis Harris poll for the magazine Valeurs Actuelles, carried out in late November, showed 73 percent of those asked disapproved of Juppe, up from 69 percent the previous month. Twenty percent approved of him against 24 percent in October.

Chirac's popularity also slumped. Sixty-four percent of those asked had a bad opinion of him, against 60 percent in late October. Twenty-nine percent approved of him, against 33 percent a month earlier.

The poll was carried out between November 28 and 30, the final days of a 12-day blockade of French roads by striking truckers who won government concessions on working hours, wages, and early retirement.
